newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close higher on Wall Street rises.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close higher on Wall Street rises.

text.p: Brazilian stocks rose early and stayed up, closing higher on weak volume.
Prices were boosted mainly by rises on Wall Street in a session marked by a lack of local news, brokers said.
"The Dow Jones went up but I didn't see anything else that affected the market," one dealer said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded shares rose 0.73 percent to close at 69,422 on turnover of 356.8 million reais ($343 million).
Brokers said rumors that federal telecoms giant Telebras would make an announcement about a new share issue kept investors speculating on Brazilian telecommunications shares,
Benchmark Telebras preferred rose 0.63 percent to 79.80 reais, while its common voter ended 0.41 percent higher at 73 reais.

Other telecom stocks also posted gains, but the advanced were smaller than those following Tuesday's sale of a minority stake in non-listed state-owned CRT for 54.8 percent over the base price. The CRT auction marked the opening of Brazil's telecoms sector to private capital.
Power shares followed the rising trend as the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most liquid power shares jumped 1.56 percent to end at 1,869.

The rise in the power index was led by a 2.05 percent climb in Minas Gerais State's Cemig preferred, which ended at 34.90 reais, boosted by investor interest ahead of the state's sale in coming weeks of a 33 percent stake in the firm.
